## Intent
Hypothesis: compiler auto-vectorization of the per-particle integration loop with a fused render phase can approach the streaming ceiling on low-churn workloads.

## Cache saturation
Cost FALLS from N=4000 to N=16000 (12.736→8.544 ns/p at q=0.01) as per-frame overhead amortizes, then stays FLAT through the L2→DRAM spill at N≈57456: N=16000 gives 8.544 and N=65000 (just past spill) gives 8.369 — no knee. The plateau holds to N=262000 (8.351) before a slight rise at N=4000000 (8.779). Death rate raises the floor without reshaping the curve: q=0.25 plateaus at ~13.45 ns/p versus ~8.35 at q=0.01, same flat-from-N=16000 pattern. The absence of any spill knee confirms the algo is not bandwidth-bound.

## Bandwidth
Peak is 8.74 GB/s at N=262000, q=0.01 — 34.7% of the 25.22 GB/s ceiling. Bandwidth is flat across N after amortization (8.54–8.74 GB/s from N=16000 to N=262000), inconsistent with a bandwidth-bound regime where one expects approach toward the ceiling as N grows. Death rate degrades it monotonically: 8.74 at q=0.01, 7.85 at q=0.05, 5.44 at q=0.25. The algo is compute/overhead-bound; the transition is by death rate, not N, as branchy respawn (`bl _spawn`, PRNG `fill` calls) adds per-particle cost scaling with churn.

## Assembly
The compiler vectorized across components of one particle, not across particles. `ldur q16` loads 4 floats from the 0x44-byte struct; `fmul.4s`/`fadd.4s` apply a 4-lane multiply-add. `ext.16b v18, v16, v17, #0xc` and `mov.s v18[3], v7[0]` shuffle bytes to align fields for the stride-0x44 layout. A gather appears: `ld1.s {v17}[1], [x11]` loads one float into a single lane, followed by `fmul.2s`/`fadd.2s`. Five `strb` instructions write byte-granular death flags (`strb w10, [x24, x8]`); these scatter stores plus 6 `bl` calls (`_bzero`, `_spawn`, `_splat`, PRNG `fill`) cap bandwidth at 35% of ceiling.

## Verdict
Refuted — peak bandwidth never exceeds 8.74 GB/s (34.7% of the 25.22 GB/s ceiling), with no L2-spill knee and flat bandwidth across N confirming compute/overhead-bound behavior. Component-wise vectorization with a gather (`ld1.s`) and byte-granular mask stores (`strb`) prevent streaming; death rate collapses bandwidth to 5.44 GB/s (21.6%) at q=0.25.
